messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] High error rate: repeated GPU OOMs observed in serving runtime (prefill path) — 12 container restarts in us-west-2 over last 5m. Auto-page oncall.
sre-oncall: Acked. Collecting logs now. Jumping in.
runtime-lead: Details? Is this isolated to a model or batch of pods?
sre-oncall: Seeing pattern: burst of long-context prefill requests from a single job (unknown tenant) -> prefill memory spikes -> container restarts. Crash logs: `CUDA out of memory` followed by SIGKILL in container.
mlops: Pasted log snippet: ```E1123 15:02:11.123 kernel: cudaMemcpy failed: out of memory
prefill.c: line 412: allocate_kv_cache failed size=7.8GB
container runtime: oom event -> restart```
sre-oncall: Node-level view: GPU memory pressure climbs to >95% for ~30s before restart, then pod churn. Not seeing scheduler evictions yet.
eng-platform: Any noisy neighbor or autoscaler kicks?
mlops: There was a concurrent eval job triggered around 15:00 that launched thousands of multi-turn eval requests with 64k+ token contexts. Looks like a thundering herd of prefill ops.
runtime-lead: Known risk: prefill allocs are proportional to sequence length * kv size. If many requests with large contexts hit same GPU, OOM.
sre-oncall: Immediate mitigations we can do: 1) apply admission control to throttle incoming requests with context > 16k 2) prefer smaller model variant for long-context requests 3) evict long-living KV caches on those pods 4) scale up capacity (fast, if we have spare GPUs).
eng-platform: We can push a temporary rate-limit at edge for `requests.context_tokens > 16000` in ~3m via edge rule. I can roll that in.
support-lead: We should prepare a customer-facing note in case this affects tenants. Any evidence of customer impact?
mlops: So far only internal eval job appears to be the blast. No spikes in external API errors yet, but container restarts could cause increased latency/errors if traffic routes to affected nodes.
customer-ops: We got an internal ticket from a customer in us-west complaining about intermittent 500s around 15:05 — likely related.
sre-oncall: Action: enable throttle at edge for >16k contexts (eng-platform), pin a fallback to small-encoder-1 model for requests >32k (runtime-lead), and evict idle KV caches on affected node pool (mlops). I'll also cordon the most flappy nodes to avoid noisy rescheduling.
eng-platform: Rolling edge rule now: `if request.context_tokens > 16000 -> 429 throttle, reason="prefill-oom-mitigation"` — will take 2m.
runtime-lead: Preparing a canary rollback: set model-mapping rule for requests with large_context=true -> small-encoder-1 (CPU-quantized) in 4m. That avoids big prefill allocations.
mlops: Eviction script: `kubectl exec -n runtime -c manager $POD -- /usr/local/bin/evict-kv --age 300` — running against pods in pool id gpu-prefill-3. Doing in waves to avoid simultaneous work.
sre-oncall: Cordon applied to node n-gpu-47. Scaling: requesting 2 spare gpus from autoscale pool; if delayed, fallback applies.
eng-platform: Edge rule in. First 10s telemetry shows ~3% of long-context requests rejected/429 — load down.
mlops: Started evictions; memory pressure dropping on affected pods. Container restarts stopped for now (observed 5m stability).
sre-oncall: Good sign. Keep monitoring for 15m.
support-lead: Draft customer message (short): "We're investigating increased 500 errors in us-west-2 caused by a burst of oversized context eval jobs; we've applied temporary throttling for very large requests and routed long-context calls to a smaller model to stabilize service. We're monitoring and will follow up in 30m." Approve?
runtime-lead: Approve. Add note: we recommend they retry with smaller contexts or async batching.
customer-ops: Sending customer update now.
sre-oncall: Followup telemetry: error rate back to baseline, latency improved. Node n-gpu-47 still flapping but cordoned.
eng-platform: Autoscaler granted 1 additional GPU (warmup 6m) — we relied on fallback so not needed immediately.
mlops: Postmortem notes to capture: origin = internal eval job causing thundering prefill; missing admission controls on long-context requests; inadequate KV eviction pacing; need better isolation for eval/test workloads.
sre-oncall: Next steps: 1) permanent admission control for context >32k -> route to batch queue 2) add per-tenant prefill concurrency cap 3) improve graceful fallback to small-encoder when memory tight 4) run load test simulating thundering large-context evals. Assign owners?
runtime-lead: I'll own #1 and #3. eng-platform owns #2. mlops will implement #4.
support-lead: I'll prepare a post-incident customer summary template.
incident-bot: Incident severity updated to SEVERITY-2. Fallback timeline: 00:12 to stable. Incident channel created.
sre-oncall: Thanks team. I'll keep this thread open for the 30m observation window, then we can move to postmortem. :white_check_mark:
